title: Pro Shop Store Credit: top-up balance-ceiling composition rule
content:
## Applies to
Pro Shop Store Credit: this document covers the composition rule that bounds how much of a top-up's combined figure (standing amount plus any bonus) is actually credited, for every tier of this product.

## Basis
Once the top-up's combined figure (the tier's own standing top-up figure plus any bonus) is determined, it is added to the account's current spendable balance, and the account's balance may never be carried above the tier's own ceiling on the stored balance. The space still available under that ceiling -- the difference between the ceiling and the balance the account already holds -- sets the most that may be credited on this top-up: only the portion of the combined figure that still fits within that remaining space is credited, and whatever would carry the balance beyond the ceiling is not accepted onto the account. This bounding is applied once, at the point the amount to be credited is finally determined, and that figure is rounded to two decimal places at that same point -- it is never rounded separately at an earlier step and then rounded again.

Before a top-up can add anything under this ceiling, the account must already have space remaining beneath it; where the account already sits at or above the ceiling, none of a further top-up's combined figure is accepted, and it is the account's own balance standing at the moment of the request that this bounding reads.

## Timing of the balance this ceiling reads
The account's balance, and the space still available under the ceiling, are read exactly as they stand at the moment this top-up is priced -- neither is read as of some earlier or later moment. Where a pending reversal of an earlier top-up is due to post to the same account around the same visit, that reversal's own effect on the balance must already be reflected before this reading is treated as final: once such a reversal posts, it lowers the account's balance and thereby increases the space still available under the ceiling. A reading taken before an already-due reversal of this kind has posted does not yet reflect the account's true standing, and understates the space actually available for this top-up.

## Points of judgement
Were the combined figure simply credited in full without regard to the ceiling, an account already near its tier's ceiling could be pushed above it; this composition rule exists precisely so that never happens -- whatever exceeds the remaining space is left off the account rather than credited and then corrected afterward.
